frontier.hypothesis: One of the allocnos this grind has never independently verified against target's bytes is mis-counted, and once it is corrected out2 at 3 refs / 714 is admissible without any reference lift at all.
frontier.mechanism: E-s28-2's hosting rule makes every flow reference count falsifiable from target's own instruction stream: a local's reg_n_refs must decompose into emitted insns with that hard register, shape-A single-use copies, and shape-B `X + constant` argument/address expressions. The model asserts a1/a2 = 16 refs / live 99, i = 10 / 97-98, tbl = 6 / 47 on the V15a chassis; none of those has ever been checked against target the way $s6 was checked this session.
frontier.next_probe: Count $s1, $s2, $s4 and $s5 occurrences in asm/funcs/func_80041188.s and decompose each count into the three hosting categories. Any allocno whose model count exceeds what target can host is a mis-modelled priority; recompute the seat order with the corrected counts and check whether out2 at 714 lands in $s6 under it. This is a pure read plus arithmetic — no build — and it either finds the error or hardens the whole model.

frontier.hypothesis: With the reference axis provably closed, out2's LIVE LENGTH is the only surviving dial on this chassis: at 3 references out2 outranks pa4 (1473) iff live <= 20, and the only definition site that reaches live 21 is inside loop1.
frontier.mechanism: pri = floor_log2(3)*3*10000/live = 30000/live, so live <= 20 clears pa4 while staying under stptr2's 2500 only for live >= 12. s12 measured an in-loop1 definition at 4 refs / live 21 = 3809 and s23 killed the site because loop1's EBB then reaches block 2 and cse1 rewrites `out3 = pa4 + 0x20` into `out3 = out2` (manufacturing the residual move). The unexamined sub-case is a definition placed AFTER out2's last use in loop1, where the value cse1 carries into block 2 may no longer be the one block 2 needs.
